title: RF-DETR-N vs YOLOv9-C: benchmark on COCO
dek: YOLOv9-C leads by 5.7 mAP points at 640 px, but RF-DETR-N at 384 px pulls ahead on Jetson Orin and Raspberry Pi 5.
author: Vision Analysis

blocks.text: YOLOv9-C is the more accurate detector, 57.1 vs 51.4 mAP@50-95 against RF-DETR-N on an RTX 5070 Ti in PyTorch. The resolutions differ: RF-DETR-N runs at 384 px and YOLOv9-C at 640 px, each at its author default, so read this as a deployment comparison. YOLOv9-C also edges the PyTorch speed test, 42.3 vs 39.5 FPS, but RF-DETR-N is faster on Jetson Orin and Raspberry Pi 5. RF-DETR-N holds a smaller footprint, 151 vs 241 MB peak VRAM.

RF-DETR-N (30.47M parameters, Apache-2.0) and YOLOv9-C (25.5M, MIT) evaluate on COCO val2017 at different input sizes: RF-DETR-N at 384 px, YOLOv9-C at 640 px, each at the author default. Both have verified rows on desktop GPU, Jetson Orin, and Raspberry Pi 5.

blocks.caption: Accuracy vs parameters on COCO val2017. RF-DETR-N and YOLOv9-C highlighted against the full set.

blocks.text: mAP is shown in percent form. YOLOv9-C measures 57.1 mAP@50-95 to RF-DETR-N's 51.4, a 5.7 point gap. The gap widens on small objects: YOLOv9-C leads 39.3 vs 27.7 mAP_small, a 29.55% relative difference.

In PyTorch on the RTX 5070 Ti, YOLOv9-C runs 42.3 FPS to RF-DETR-N's 39.5. YOLOv9-C keeps the lead on both TensorRT builds: 76.7 vs 67.6 FPS on FP32, 74.7 vs 58.3 on FP16. On ONNX Runtime the two are close, 63.5 vs 65.7.
The desktop order reverses on edge hardware. On Jetson Orin, RF-DETR-N runs 10.2 FPS to YOLOv9-C's 6.4. On Raspberry Pi 5 it is 2.1 vs 0.5. For low-power targets RF-DETR-N is the faster model.

Pick YOLOv9-C for desktop or GPU deployment and for accuracy, especially on small objects. Pick RF-DETR-N for Jetson- or Pi-class edge hardware, where it runs faster at 384 px, and when VRAM is tight, 151 vs 241 MB. Both ship under permissive licenses.

# pip install libreyolo
from libreyolo import LibreYOLO

rfdetr = LibreYOLO("LibreRFDETRn.pt")  # 30.47M params, 51.4 mAP@50-95
yolo9 = LibreYOLO("LibreYOLO9c.pt")    # 25.5M params, 57.1 mAP@50-95

results = yolo9("image.jpg")
